provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the original frame, each 2x2 square of colour 5 gets four diagonal corner markers one step outside its bounding box: 1 at top-left, 2 at top-right, 3 at bottom-left and 4 at bottom-right. The factory writes each corner as a direction vector (sy, sx) in {-1,+1}^2 and pushes it through the visible transform. For d4>=4 it first applies a horizontal flip, (dy,dx)->(dy,-dx). It then applies d4%4 clockwise rotations, (dy,dx)->(dx,-dy). The result maps each visible diagonal direction to the constant palette[original marker colour]. The emitted program works directly on the visible grid. It finds 4-connected components of colour palette[5] and takes each bounding box. At each diagonal corner it places the matching marker colour, but only when the cell is in bounds and still background (palette[0]). Squares are processed independently, so their order does not matter.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the constructor's domain: a background of palette[0] with solid 2x2 squares of palette[5]. It matches squares by that colour, not by inferring roles from the demonstrations. It does not analyse the generator's own spacing guarantees. The bounds check and the write-only-onto-background check are kept as safeguards, matching the archived solver. No constructor defects or fixture contradictions were found. All fixtures follow the uniform corner-marker rule.
